title: Are Yields Rising Too Fast For Banks?
gist: US bank stocks fell 7.5% since September while the S&P 500 gained 1%, apparently on fears that yields are rising too fast; Gavekal expects the concern to prove short-lived around upcoming earnings.

insights.claim: US bank stocks (S&P 500 bank index) are down 7.5% since the start of September against a 1% gain in the S&P 500, despite an inflationary boom that should favor lenders.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Banks have de-rated against the market going into earnings.

insights.claim: A gradual rise in yields helps banks via loan pricing and securities returns, but a rapid rise as in 2021-22 can break things and hurt the sector, which is likely what equity investors fear.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Pace of yield rise, not level, drives bank risk.

insights.claim: Gavekal sees reasons the bank-stock concerns will prove short-lived as US commercial banks start reporting earnings, supported by positive September growth surprises and energy-driven higher yields.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
